originals.role: String and handle bodies, method dispatch, surviving fixed-point arithmetic, coefficient tables, contracts, and histories.
MacApp globals and memory trap words.
MacApp globals and memory trap words.

changes: Munger and XMunger retain their released string-search, replacement, and handle-size bodies. Twelve explicit short branches restore the ROM encodings. The handle clone entry names omit the Trap suffix added in May 1992.

HandToHand and HandAndHand save the master-pointer byte, clear purge bit six, and restore the byte through the saved source handle. These instructions predate the HGetState, HNoPurge, and HSetState calls added in September 1986.

MethodDispatch retains the original cache and superclass search. It loads MASuperTab before searching and uses the original A5-relative dispatch branch order. The June 1986 duplicate search loop is absent.

LongMul, FixMul, and FracMul share a restored 68000 multiply body from $4157B2 through $415853. It forms the full product with four unsigned word multiplies, handles signed operands, and selects scaling and rounding by the entry point. The source history says that the old 68000 bodies were removed in October 1991; the remaining source contains 68020 replacements.

FixRatio restores the 68000 body at $41593A through $415961. It loads signed word arguments with MOVEM.W, returns 1.0 immediately when they are equal, and otherwise divides the integer and fractional parts separately. The equality path also makes 0/0 return 1.0. The shared sign and exit code survives in the release.

FixDiv and FracDiv retain the older quotient-count limit of 31 and omit the overflow handling added in November 1986. The omitted inner-loop carry test was already absent from the target ROM, despite the later date attached to its commented-out source line.

FixRound restores the earlier subtract-half path for negative input and the earlier saturation code. The source contract says to chop toward zero, but this ROM takes the signed high word without the needed correction; for example, -1.0 yields -2. The reconstruction preserves these instructions and identifies the comment mismatch.

FixATan2 retains word-sized SUBQ instructions on the extreme-negative input paths. Fix2Long and Frac2Fix retain their two word-sized rounding ADDQ instructions. The later source changed those instructions to long size.

The square-root loop, trigonometric polynomials and coefficient tables, extended conversions, and remaining fixed-point conversions retain their released bodies. Table references and two FracMul calls use explicit PC-relative addressing. Long branches remain explicit where the earlier shared multiply body changes the distance.

The original file attribution, 1985 history, routine contracts, inline comments, and conditional export names remain where they apply. Corrected comments identify the sign byte, argument offsets, FracDiv result format, and two leading fractional bits. Original source spelling cannot be recovered for the removed arithmetic bodies.

restored_68000_ranges.purpose: Shared LongMul, FracMul, and FixMul body.

historical_limits: Exact assembly establishes instructions and data. It does not execute the arithmetic over all inputs or recover the wording of the removed source.
